summary_oneline: Add NOT (@!) and OR-if-not-exists (@$) JSONB dict-filter operators to the PostgreSQL parser, mirroring the @>| pattern across the Cython and Rust builders.

constraints.statement: JSONB operators are keys INSIDE a column's dict value ({"col": {"@op": ...}}), never top-level where_cond keys; the caller loop validates each where_cond key as a safe SQL identifier and silently skips non-identifier keys such as a literal "@!".
constraints.implication: the ticket's literal example shape ({"@!": [...]} at top level) does not fit the existing mechanism; the consistent shape is {"<jsonb_col>": {"@!": [...]}}

constraints.statement: filter_conditions() prefers the Rust fast-path and silently falls back to Cython only on exception; a mis-rendered (not raising) Rust path wins.
constraints.implication: both builders must learn @!/@$ in the same change, and the Rust crate must be rebuilt (maturin develop) before tests

constraints.statement: jsonb_condition dispatches on the FIRST operator key only and drops dicts mixing operator and plain keys (operators != len(value)); a dict carrying both @! and @$ renders only the first today.
constraints.implication: supporting the ticket example (both operators in one dict) requires either multi-operator AND-composition or documenting single-operator-per-dict

constraints.statement: All rendered conditions are joined with AND; values go through pg_literal (brace/backslash-safe E'...' quoting) to survive later format_map passes.
constraints.implication: new renderers must reuse pg_literal/jsonb_operand exactly like jsonb_any_of_condition

constraints.statement: Every existing JSONB filter case is tested through BOTH code paths via PATHS parametrization; commit 8936386 (the AND/OR support) is the exact structural precedent.
constraints.implication: the change must ship dual-path tests in tests/test_pgsql_jsonb_filters.py, same as the @>| commit

unknowns.question: What exact SQL semantics should '@$' ('OR if not exists') have for {"col": {"@$": [a, b]}}?
plausible_answers: (NOT col @> a) OR (NOT col @> b) — row lacks at least one of the operands (dual of @!)
col IS NULL OR col = '{}'::jsonb OR (col @> a OR col @> b) — match if the JSONB is absent/empty, else behave like @>|
NOT (col @> a AND col @> b) — row does not contain ALL operands
unknowns.user_answer: OR-of-NOT: {"col": {"@$": [a, b]}} renders ((NOT col @> 'a'::jsonb) OR (NOT col @> 'b'::jsonb)); additionally, one dict may carry both @! and @$, with the rendered groups AND-ed (dispatch extended to iterate all operator keys).

unknowns.question: Is the intended filter shape per-column ({"course_data": {"@!": [...]}}) — consistent with @>/@>| — or literally top-level operator keys in where_cond as the ticket example shows (which would require extending the caller loop and identifier validation)?
plausible_answers: per-column, like the existing operators — the example omitted the column name
top-level grouping keys — a new mechanism spanning multiple columns
unknowns.user_answer: Per-column, like the existing operators — the ticket example omitted the column name. Only jsonb_condition (both builders) changes.

unknowns.question: Must one dict be able to carry BOTH @! and @$ simultaneously (as in the example), AND-ing the two rendered groups, or is one operator per dict acceptable (current dispatch uses only the first key)?
plausible_answers: both in one dict, AND-ed — extend dispatch to iterate all operator keys
one operator per dict is fine — document the restriction
unknowns.user_answer: Both in one dict, AND-ed — extend the dispatch to iterate all operator keys instead of only the first. @! renders the none-of form NOT (col @> a OR col @> b).
